title: Workload Portrait & Sampler Playbook
author: Daniela Ruiz
content:
Overview

This playbook prescribes a compact, reproducible method for building workload portraits and converting those portraits into sampler policies used by the runtime. The goal is simple: capture the most diagnostically valuable traces given constrained storage and ingestion budgets, prioritize SLO-sensitive cohorts, and validate sampling choices via shadow replay before production rollout.

Audience

Runtime engineers, SREs, performance researchers, and platform product engineers who are responsible for profiling, kernel scheduling validation, and observability.

Goals

- Produce workload portraits: histograms, canonical traces, and impact statements per route/cohort.
- Generate versioned sampler policies that map cohorts to sample rates, triggers, and retention tiers.
- Validate sampling and capture fidelity through mirrored collection and shadow replay.

Core concepts (short)

- Workload portrait: short JSON/YAML summary containing p50/p95/p99 of sequence length, tokens, KV cache hit rate, and 3 canonical traces.
- Cohort: predicate for sampling (route, model, customer_tier, seq_bucket).
- Sampler policy: control-plane artifact (YAML) mapping cohorts -> sample_rate + triggers.
- Shadow replay: deterministic replay of captured traces against baseline and candidate kernels.

Principles

1) Discover before capturing: use cheap histograms (5m granularity) for discovery; escalate to full traces only where needed.
2) Keep policies limited and auditable: small set of cohort predicates that are easy to reason about and versioned in git.
3) Validate in staging: mirror, replay, and run explicit hypothesis tests before any policy changes go wide.
4) Privacy-first: redact/pseudonymize textual content by default; keep provenance metadata for debugging.

Process (step-by-step)

1) Discovery (7-14 days)
- Select anchor routes: 8-12 routes covering ~75% of token volume or SLA-bound endpoints. Include a mix of PLG and enterprise.
- Deploy histogram exporter (5m buckets) to collect seq_len, tokens_per_request, kv_cache_hit_pct, and response_size. Collect 14 days.
- Perform brief owner interviews (15-30m) to capture SLOs, fidelity tolerances, and known hotspots.

Deliverables: portrait.csv (route, p50/p95/p99 seq_len, tokens, owner, sla_flag), owner-notes.md.

2) Portrait synthesis (2-4 days)
- Cluster histogram vectors and business attributes into 3-6 portraits (examples: interactive-short, streaming-multi-turn, batch-embeddings).
- For each portrait produce: one-line impact statement, primary SLO metric, cost-sensitivity score (1-5), and sample density recommendation.

3) Sampler policy design (2-3 days)
- Baseline discovery rate: 0.05% to 0.5% depending on token volume.
- Portrait-driven rules: prioritize SLO-bound cohorts with higher baseline rates and escalation triggers.
- Retention tiers: full traces (14d default), escalated retention (up to 90d with approvals), aggregated histograms (365d).

Example sampler YAML (human readable)

sampler_version: 4
default_sample_rate: 0.0005  # 0.05%
cohorts:
  - id: interactive_short
    match: "route =~ '^chat:' and seq_len < 256"
    sample_rate: 0.01
    triggers:
      - metric: latency_p95_ms
        threshold: 250
        action: escalate_to_full_capture
  - id: streaming_multi_turn
    match: "archetype == 'streaming-multi-turn'"
    sample_rate: 0.005
    triggers:
      - metric: node_memory_util
        threshold: 0.9
        action: increase_sample_rate_to_0.05_ttl_180m
  - id: batch_embeddings
    match: "route =~ '^embed:'"
    sample_rate: 0.0002
    triggers:
      - metric: job_failure_count
        threshold: 1
        action: capture_failed_jobs_full

Implementation checklist (ops)

- Tagging: ensure request envelopes include route, archetype, customer_tier, seq_len_bucket.
- Provenance: every sampled record must include request_id, kernel_hash, node_id, model_variant, sampler_policy_version.
- Node-local sampler: a lightweight plugin that applies control-plane YAML and exposes /_internal/sampler/health and /_internal/sampler/policy endpoints.
- Telemetry: emit sample_rate_by_cohort, sample_loss_rate, policy_sync_lag to observability.
- Redaction: default pipeline must remove/replace any user prompt text fields before storage.

Validation (mirror + replay)

Stage A: Mirror (72h)
- Mirror sampled captures to validation cluster. Keep copies short-lived.

Stage B: Shadow replay
- Replay traces deterministically against baseline kernel and candidate kernels.
- Compute deltas: latency_p50/p95/p99, memory_alloc_per_request, token_cost_per_request, error_rate.

Acceptance thresholds

- SLO portraits: p95 delta <= 5% AND p99 delta <= 10%.
- Memory-sensitive portraits: OOM increase <= 0.1% absolute.
- Cost-sensitive portraits: token_cost delta <= 7%.

If a portrait fails validation, increase sample density for that portrait and re-run mirror + replay.

Operational runbook (abridged)

Trigger conditions:
- Coverage drop: sampler coverage decrease > 50% in 30 minutes.
- Sampler errors: sampler_error_rate > 0.2%.
- Config drift: policy_sync_lag > 2 minutes on >10% of nodes.

Oncall triage steps:
1) Check control-plane rollout logs and policy versions.
2) Query node sampler health: curl http://<node>:PORT/_internal/sampler/health
3) If coverage loss confirmed: enable emergency_full_capture for affected cohorts (TTL: 6h) and page runtime team.
4) Collect trace ids, attach to incident ticket, and escalate to runtime-observability.

CLI Snippets

- Emergency full capture via control-plane: 
  rctl sampler trigger --policy emergency_full --cohort interactive_short --ttl 360

- List sampled traces for route: 
  rctl traces list --route chat:widget --since 24h --limit 500

- Check node policy version: 
  curl http://<node>:PORT/_internal/sampler/policy | jq .version

Dashboards (recommended panels)

- Coverage matrix: cohort x hour showing sample_rate and total_traces.
- Sampler health: policy_sync_lag, sampler_errors_per_min, sample_loss_rate.
- Portrait regression panel: p95/p99 deltas by portrait.
- Cost vs visibility: daily storage cost for traces vs number of portraits captured.

Configuration & cost guideline (summary)

Item | Default | Rationale
Default discovery sample rate | 0.05% | Low-cost discovery for high-volume routes
Full-trace retention | 14 days | Enough for incident triage and replay
Histogram retention | 365 days | Useful for trend/seasonality analysis
Estimate storage | ~$90/day per 10k full traces | Varies with compression and redaction

Privacy and security

- Redact full prompt text fields and store only hashed identifiers for join operations.
- Restricted customers: capture only aggregated telemetry unless explicit approvals are present; always enforce KMS encryption for persisted traces.

Ownership & escalation

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime
- Observability steward: runtime-observability
- Oncall: eng-sre
- Escalation path: runtime-oncall page -> #runtime-urgent -> create incident via opsbot

Experiment template (compact)

Hypothesis: "Kernel change X will reduce p95 by >=6% for interactive-short portrait."
Design: bump interactive_short sample_rate to 1% for 72h and mirror captured traces to staging.
Success: p95 reduction >= 6% OR p99 reduction >= 4% AND no OOM increase > 0.05%.
Rollout: successful experiments -> canary 5% traffic 24h -> 25% 48h -> 100%. Failures -> revert and document.
